title: Naval on founders, skills, habits and happiness: The Tim Ferriss Show (2016)
summary: Naval explains what he looks for in founders (intelligence, energy, integrity), why conventional wisdom in startups is always wrong, and how to guard your time. He also covers habit building, reading old books, and happiness as a skill built through awareness and acceptance.

principles.text: Back founders with intelligence, energy and integrity; high intelligence plus low integrity is a smart crook.
principles.quote: if you have someone who's high intelligence and high energy but they're low Integrity what you've got is a hardworking smart crook

principles.text: Great new companies look strange; conventional wisdom in startups always gets blown up, so evaluate each deal on its own merits.
principles.quote: the great new companies always look really strange they don't look very much like the previous companies

principles.text: Venture returns come from being right when everyone else is wrong, and winners overwhelm losses, so focus on upside.
principles.quote: in this industry you get paid for being right when everybody else is wrong

principles.text: Guard your time more carefully than your money; avoid advisory roles that eat time.
principles.quote: guard your time carefully Right Guard your time more carefully than you guard your money

principles.text: Only work with people you genuinely like; no amount of money is worth spending a decade with downers.
principles.quote: you just have to make sure you actually genuinely like these people you don't consider it work to have to answer a phone call or take a meeting or spend time with them

principles.text: Learning to read is the ultimate meta skill; read old books and don't feel obliged to finish any.
principles.quote: when you're talking about solving old problems the older the problem the older the solution
